entities.evidence: In אַנְשֵׁי סְדֹם, “the men of Sodom,” סְדֹם names the city whose inhabitants the verse describes.
לַיַהְוֶה names Yahweh as the God against whom the men of Sodom sinned.

analysis.evidence: The place name סְדֹם completes the construct phrase אַנְשֵׁי סְדֹם, “the men of Sodom.” The plural predicates רָעִים and וְחַטָּאִים describe those inhabitants.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וְ is prefixed to אַנְשֵׁי, the irregular masculine plural construct form of אִישׁ.
analysis.sense: the men of a leader or place; a citizen, a follower

draft.change: Add a standalone place-name article for סְדֹם, keyed by its own consonants סדמ. The supplied root סגר does not account for this form.
draft.definition: סְדֹם is the Hebrew name of the city of Sodom.
draft.evidence: Genesis 10:19 names Sodom alongside Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboiim in its description of Canaanite territory.

analysis.evidence: In וְאַנְשֵׁי סְדֹם, “and the men of Sodom,” סְדֹם completes the construct phrase by naming the city whose men the verse describes as wicked.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: רָעִים describes the men of Sodom. The coordinated וְחַטָּאִים, “and sinners,” confirms that the adjective describes their moral character.
analysis.morphology: Masculine plural absolute adjective used predicatively of אַנְשֵׁי סְדֹם, “the men of Sodom.”
analysis.sense: evil, wicked (of persons, hearts, ways, deeds)

analysis.evidence: וְ joins חַטָּאִים to רָעִים (“wicked”). Both describe אַנְשֵׁי סְדֹם (“the men of Sodom”), and לַיַהְוֶה identifies YHWH as the one against whom they sinned.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וְ means “and.” חַטָּאִים is a masculine plural absolute adjective used substantivally as a predicate.

analysis.morphology: The prefixed preposition לַ־ ‘to, for’ introduces the proper name יַהְוֶה.
analysis.sense: Personal name of the God of Israel
